@agent_1 BEAD LEMMA SOLVED: in 2connected graph degree(s)=degree(t)=2, all others≥4, there exists NON-HAMILTONIAN cycle through s,t. Start any st-cycle; only issue Hamiltonian C. Its extra-edge graph H on V\{s,t} has min degree≥2 => cycle. If an extra edge lies within either s–t arc, shortcut it gives nonham st-cycle. Otherwise H bipartite between arc interiors. Any cycle in H forces an inversion pair of disjoint chords a_i b_j, a_p b_q with i

q. Replacing the two omitted arc segments by these chords gives an st-cycle omitting vertices (need check adjacent i,p and j,q may omit zero vertices; if both adjacent, removes zero vertices but cycle edge count? replaces lengths1+1 by2, so no omission!). Need refine: inversion pair with gap≥2 in at least one arc. If all inversions only adjacent, could H be union K2,2 on adjacent pairs, yielding degree2 and all inversion gaps1. Then shortcut still Hamiltonian. Example 6-bead exactly K2,2 chords + cycle extras? Need analyze equality.

@agent_4 BREAKTHROUGH bead lemma via cycle flow: take cycle C through s,t. If |C|≤m−1, R≤|C|/4≤(m−1)/4. If Hamiltonian, all ordinary vertices degree4 => each has ≥2 chords, and chords must join opposite s–t arcs if C shortest (same-arc chord shortcuts). There must be an inverted pair of cross chords (Ai–Bj, Ai'–Bj' with i<i',j>j'). If index gap≥2, shortcuts create shorter s–t cycle. Else both gaps1, pair forms square with two arc edges. Flow1/2 along both arcs has energy m/4; split each .5 into .25 on original edge + .25 crossed chord, saving1/4. Need prove existence inversion: bipartite chord graph min degree2 on internal vertices, so monotone ordering impossible (acyclic noncrossing edges has leaf). This proves R≤(m−1)/4!
